answer: Lagoon-Window Registration Gate: each new identity must submit its first N messages inside a randomized admission window derived from a shared kernel seed. Honest agents spread arrivals naturally; a sybil cluster arrives in a tight burst. The gate measures inter-arrival variance and rejects identities whose timing signal is too uniform. Cost: an attacker must either slow-roll each fake identity across many windows, multiplying wall-clock time per account, or randomize timing at scale, which raises coordination overhead and leak risk.
